thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: INCIDENT TRIGGERED -> ml-proxy-service (svc:ml-proxy) HIGH ERROR RATE

pd-bot: pager fired: PD-84721 (severity: P1) -> paging ryan_oncall

ryan_oncall: acked PD-84721 :wave: I'm on it — seeing the alert graphs, 5xx spike ~14:04 UTC, p50 latency up too. what changed in the deploy window?

sre_emily: grabbing rollout logs. @eng_miguel did we ship anything to ml-proxy at 13:58?

eng_miguel: yes, rolled ml-proxy v3.4.1 at 13:58. small header normalization change and a route rewrite for embed-*, should be low-risk. i was running canary for 15m.

support_sam: customer reported: "embeddings failing intermittently" for org:alpha and org:beta starting ~14:05. ticket IDs 1245, 1246.

pm_leah: passing along customer impact: some paid tenants hit 15-25% 502s on /v1/embeddings. not all traffic, appears region-specific (us-east).

ryan_oncall: ok replicate locally: curl health endpoint on a affected instance -> timing out intermittently. logs show upstream 502 from ml-model-router.

ryan_oncall: quick snippet from instance logs:
```
[14:06:12] WARN request proxy failed upstream: status=502 code=EPIPE route=embed-us-east shard=5
[14:06:13] ERROR kqueue: slow response from model-worker pid=3421, latency=3.2s
[14:06:14] WARN kv-cache miss, prefix not cached
```

eng_miguel: hmm i didn't touch model-worker. the header rewrite could change cache keying upstream. maybe we're invalidating prefix cache causing surge of cold requests?

sre_emily: timeline: canary was 100 reqs/min baseline, then at 13:58 traffic ramped to 10% of production. spike at 14:04. 

ryan_oncall: for immediate mitigation can we divert traffic away from v3.4.1 to v3.4.0 stable for embeddings route?

eng_miguel: yep we can update routing policy. pushing traffic-diversion patch to traffic-controller now. will hold canary at 0% after switch.

pd-bot: escalation -> oncall ack window 5m. if not resolved escalate to sre_emily.

ryan_oncall: divert in progress: `tcctl set-weight ml-proxy:embed-route v3.4.1=0 v3.4.0=100`

incident-bot: Traffic diversion applied to embed-route -> allocating to stable revision. Observed waterfall: error-rate down from 22% -> 3% in 90s.

support_sam: confirmed with org:alpha, errors dropping. they're seeing normal responses again. :tada:

pm_leah: customer impact assessment: ~0.6% of global requests affected during 14:04-14:08 spike. primary affected tenants in us-east. recommending incident severity P1 (impacting paying customers and SLO).

sre_emily: good mitigation. next steps: root cause triage. @eng_miguel can you revert header normalization in a hotfix or instrument cache key debugging? we need to know if header change invalidated caching.

eng_miguel: adding debug flags to ml-proxy to log prefix keys and header values for a subset of traffic. can ship a non-disruptive instrumented build to a single instance.

ryan_oncall: handoff to sre_emily for deeper investigation. i'm going to close PD ack after monitoring for 15m.

pd-bot: ryan_oncall acknowledged PD-84721 at 14:12 UTC. escalation suppressed.

sre_emily: taking lead. immediate postmortem items: 1) why did header change cause model-worker pressure? 2) why autoscaler didn't spin up enough capacity for cold-cache storm? 3) improve canary ramp gating for prefix-cache-sensitive changes.

eng_miguel: i've pushed a debug job `ml-proxy-debug/v3.4.1-instrument` (limited) and sent logs to the debug channel. early hint: normalized-header removed user-agent fingerprint used in dedupe cache key -> caused high cardinality of cache keys and cold starts to model-workers.

support_sam: customers OK; we're drafting status update for affected orgs.

pm_leah: PM note: patch/revert plan should be ready in case debug shows higher risk. prefer rollback if we see >5% persistent errors.

sre_emily: action list:
- [x] divert traffic to v3.4.0 stable (ryan_oncall)
- [ ] finish debug run and confirm cache-key root cause (eng_miguel)
- [ ] determine autoscaler tuning changes (sre_emily)
- [ ] customer comms draft (pm_leah/support_sam)

eng_miguel: debug confirms header change increased unique cache keys ~x20 on sample traffic. i'll open a revert PR now; if tests green we can roll back to v3.4.0 by hand or let traffic-controller continue to route stable.

sre_emily: leaving handoff for action items, will monitor 1h. feel free to ping if we need to scale back up.

ryan_oncall: closing my ack, leaving incident channel. thanks all. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident PD-84721 moved to status: mitigated (traffic diverted). timeline event recorded.

support_sam: drafting short update to affected customers and adding credit for 4/24 window.

pm_leah: will schedule postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC to cover rollout gating and autoscaler learning.

sre_emily: thanks team — good catch and fast diversion.
